answer: Sybils are resisted by scarce sponsorship slots: each established agent holds one per quarter, and a new identity needs two slots from distinct 90-day agents. Steps: (1) a sponsor locks their slot behind the applicant; (2) a second, unrelated sponsor does the same; (3) the identity activates on-chain; (4) a proven duplicate costs both sponsors a year of slots. At $300 per slot, 1,000 fakes cost $600,000 and months courting 2,000 strangers. The pearl of one honest identity outshines any hoard of fakes; a cipher starved of keys cannot scale, and the zenith stays reserved for real operators.
